Where the terrain shades itself

Source: R/shade.R
cast_shade.Rd

Cast shadows for one sun position, by a single directional sweep over the grid: a "shadow surface" is carried along the light's direction, dropping by step * tan(elevation) each cell, and a cell is in shadow where the surface arriving at it is above the ground. With far, a coarse surrounding grid casts first (with earth curvature) and its shadow surface comes in over z from distant ridges.

Usage

cast_shade(
  z,
  extent = NULL,
  azimuth,
  elevation,
  far = NULL,
  far_extent = NULL,
  convergence = 0
)

Arguments

z

matrix of heights, row 1 at the north edge, square cells; or the result of gdalraster::read_ds() (a vector with a gis attribute), in which case extent is taken from it

extent

c(xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax) of z

azimuth

sun azimuth, degrees clockwise from true north

elevation

sun elevation, degrees above the horizon

far, far_extent

optional coarser grid surrounding z (and its extent), for terrain further out; its cells that touch z are skipped

convergence

grid azimuth of true north (meridian convergence, degrees), added to azimuth; 0 for a grid aligned with true north. In polar stereographic (EPSG:3031, EPSG:3413 style) it is the longitude, or minus it in the north

Value

logical matrix like z, TRUE in shadow (all TRUE when the sun is down), with attribute extent

Examples

z <- volcano[nrow(volcano):1, ncol(volcano):1]
ex <- c(2667400, 2668010, 6478700, 6479570)
s <- cast_shade(z, ex, azimuth = 300, elevation = 15)
mean(s)
#> [1] 0.2095346
if (requireNamespace("ximage", quietly = TRUE)) {
  ximage::ximage(z, extent = ex, col = grey.colors(64), asp = 1)
  ximage::ximage(s * 1, extent = ex, add = TRUE, col = c(NA, adjustcolor("navy", 0.5)))
}
